units.function: Reads Paperclip configuration, normalizes and de-duplicates one hostname into server.allowedHostnames, updates configuration metadata, writes the file and tells the operator to restart; it warns that enforcement applies only in authenticated/private mode.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI configuration command -> hostname normalizer and config store -> server private-hostname guard after restart. It changes inbound server Host policy only and does not constrain CLI/client outbound API origins, credential audiences, DNS resolution or TLS.
units.keyDataModels: server.allowedHostnames string set; deploymentMode/exposure; config metadata updatedAt/source. There is no canonical origin, port/scheme/certificate, IDNA form, resolved-address policy, proxy trust, change actor/approval or stable command-result model.
units.lifecycle: Resolve/read config -> normalize input -> lower/trim existing values -> add and sort -> stamp metadata -> rewrite config -> print existed/added/restart messages -> warn when outside authenticated/private profile. No dry run, removal, rollback, lock, atomic compare-and-swap, runtime reload verification or audit event is present.
units.testAssessment: The previously completed allowed-hostname test was reused without rereading: focused Vitest passed 1/1 and proves scheme/port/lowercase normalization plus duplicate suppression. Existing server guard assessments prove the basic private-profile predicate and allow/reject paths, but omit actual adversarial Host parsing dimensions including trailing-dot/IDNA/IPv6, malformed/multiple Host, proxy headers, wildcard/subdomain, DNS rebinding and authorization/audit of allowlist changes. CLI storage atomicity/permissions/symlink and concurrent updates remain untested.
units.designRationale: A dedicated remediation command is safer and less error-prone than asking operators to edit JSON manually, and normalization/de-duplication produces deterministic config. Restricting the guard to private authenticated deployments reflects an intended deployment policy but is not a general network trust boundary.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs coherent inbound Host/origin/proxy protection and outbound egress-origin pinning across managed and self-hosted profiles, with authorized configuration changes and runtime verification.
units.companyOsFit: Reference the operator workflow, not the implementation. Define canonical EndpointPolicy and TrustedOrigin/AllowedHost value objects with IDNA/IPv6/port/proxy semantics; separate inbound Host/CSRF policy from outbound credential audience/egress policy. Apply changes through an authenticated application command with preview, actor, reason, revision CAS, audit event, reload/restart status and rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: Changing an inbound trust allowlist can expand who reaches the control plane, yet this local mutation records only source=configure and no accountable human, approval or reason. A hostname entry must not confer Company/Principal authorization; identity and role checks remain independent.

units.securityFindings: This command does not mitigate the confirmed outbound context/apiBase credential-exfiltration chain. It rewrites security configuration without actor authorization, revision conflict detection or atomic/locked storage and follows config-store filesystem semantics. Runtime enforcement requires restart but is not verified. The command itself warns enforcement is limited to authenticated/private, leaving other profiles dependent on different controls. Host allowlisting alone does not handle DNS rebinding, proxy trust, CSRF Origin, TLS/certificate identity or outbound credential destination.
